questions: If a group of three bits contains a tie (i.e., exactly one 0 and two 1s or two 0s and one 1), which value is considered to appear most frequently for determining C_i?
Are the bits in the input string A given without spaces (e.g., "01011") or separated by spaces as shown in the format description?
Must the output be a single integer followed by a newline, or are additional whitespaces allowed?
Is the string indexing 1‑based as described, and does the grouping always start at B₁, B₂, B₃, then B₄, B₅, B₆, etc., without any offset?
When changing bits to achieve a different A′₁, may we change any bits of A, including those that belong to the same triple, or is there a limit on how many bits can be altered within a single group?
Should we consider the possibility of changing zero bits (i.e., answer 0) if A′₁ can already be flipped by the definition of the operation, or is the minimum always at least 1?
Are there any constraints on the input size beyond N ≤ 13 that could affect memory or time limits (e.g., maximum total input length, time limit per test case)?
In the case where multiple minimal sets of bit flips exist, does the problem require any specific tie‑breaking rule for which set to choose, or is only the count of flips needed?

inline_prompts:
For a binary string B = B_1 B_2 \dots B_{3^n} of length 3^n (n \geq 1), we define an operation to obtain a binary string C = C_1 C_2 \dots C_{3^{n-1}} of length 3^{n-1} as follows:
- Partition the elements of B into groups of 3 and take the value from each group. That is, for i=1,2,\dots,3^{n-1}, let C_i be the value that appears most frequently among B_{3i-2}, B_{3i-1}, and B_{3i}, with a tie being resolved by choosing the value that appears first in the group (i.e., the majority is always 2 out of 3, so a tie can't occur among 3 bits).
You are given a binary string A = A_1 A_2 \dots A_{3^N} of length 3^N. Let A' = A'_1 be the length-1 string obtained by applying the above operation to A.
Determine the minimum number of elements of A that must be changed (from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0) in order to change the value of A'_1.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N
A_1 A_2 \dots A_{3^N}
Output
Print the answer.
Constraints
- N is an integer with 1 \leq N \leq 13.
- A is a string of length 3^N consisting of 0 and 1.
